candidate.answerReason: The center-to-chord distances are 6 and 15 feet. The center distance can be 21 or 9 feet; 21 is the listed possible value.

methods.label: Use the half-chord
methods.explanation:
Let \(P,Q\) be the common chord's endpoints and \(M\) its midpoint. Then \(PM=8\) feet. In each circle, the line from its center to the midpoint of this chord is perpendicular to the chord. Thus both centers lie on the same perpendicular through \(M\).

Joining either center to \(P\) forms a right triangle with one leg \(8\) and hypotenuse equal to that circle's radius. The two distances from the centers to \(M\) are therefore
\[
\sqrt{10^2-8^2}=6,
\qquad
\sqrt{17^2-8^2}=15.
\]
If the centers lie on opposite sides of \(M\), their distance is \(6+15=21\) feet. If they lie on the same side, their distance is \(15-6=9\) feet. Both arrangements are possible: placing the centers at these distances along the perpendicular leaves \(P\) and \(Q\) on both circles.

Thus \(\boxed{21\text{ feet}}\) is a possible center distance, choice B.
